subject: research/mimic-codeloop
professional: a senior ML / program-synthesis researcher who reviews for NeurIPS or ICSE (LLM code generation with execution feedback, LLM-guided program search); first checks: is there a baseline that can move at the chosen budget, how many seeds and what uncertainty, are failures of the harness (sandbox, token cap, no retry) separated from failures of the model, and is the nearest prior work (FunSearch, ELM/OpenELM, Eureka, Self-Debug, Reflexion, CodeT) cited and compared

evidence.correctness: The reported numbers reproduce. (a) report.py and experiments/figure.py rerun on a copy of research/{mimic-codeloop,mimic-cursor,_shared} in the scratchpad with /usr/bin/python3.13: results.txt, results.json and figure.svg byte-identical to the committed files. (b) My own script reading results/run_*_0.json directly (no import of report.py) gives blind: 24 candidates, banned token 10, does not load 3 (SyntaxError 1, ValueError 1, NameError 1), invalid-after-run 4, valid 7; feedback: banned 7, does not load 7 (SyntaxError 6, NameError 1), invalid 4, valid 6; totals 17/10/8 of 48 as README:26 says. Reference AUROC is exactly 1.0 at every round 0-6 in both runs. (c) The component-search comparison recomputed from mimic-cursor/results/run_blind_*.json and run_d2i_*.json at round 6: blind values 0.99825-1.0 (mean 0.99954), d2i 0.99945-1.0 (mean 0.99990), consistent with '1.000 (0.999 to 1.000)'. (d) README:27's claim that neither final program has pixel rounding or a human event clock, which the author checked only by reading, I measured by running both final programs through sandbox.run on 200 random start/end pairs: 100% of interior points non-integer, the only event interval 16.0 ms. Partial: the blind final program is not 'a random direction added to a line' but a straight line at a 0-20 degree heading that ignores the target, so the sandbox's endpoint pin makes the last step a jump of median 1.25 chords. Runtime claims (about 1 min per candidate, about 30 min per run) match the logged seconds (1,543 s and 1,938 s for 24 candidates). The experiment itself could not be rerun (torch, transformers, sklearn absent; a 1.5B model on CPU).
evidence.completeness: What the README lists exists: codeloop.py, sandbox.py, report.py, figure, 2 result files with every candidate's outcome and the final program, 4 tests as stated, live page https://marisstella.app/research/mimic-codeloop/ returns 200. But the designed experiment ran one third: codeloop.py:199 defaults to 3 seeds and the README says 3 were planned, 1 ran. Candidate source code and model replies are not saved (codeloop.py:173-185 records only valid/score/error), so the failure breakdown that is the study's 'informative number' cannot be inspected; the banned token is not logged (sandbox.py:263-264). No blog post in docs/posts and no entry in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` in research/mimic-codeloop: 4 tests OK in 1.0 s (bare python3 fails: no numpy, while README:43 says `python3 -m unittest`). Tests cover only sandbox.py. Mutations via quality_mutate.py: time-not-increasing `<= 0` -> `< 0` caught; failure cap MAX_FAIL -> 0.5 in codeloop.py:163 SURVIVED; report.py:49 outcome label collapsing 'crashes or copies' into 'valid' SURVIVED (it would change the headline valid share); dropping the endpoint pin at sandbox.py:79 SURVIVED (the test generator already ends at the target). codeloop.py and report.py have no tests and no test pins a results.txt number. 3 of 4 mutants survive.
evidence.craft: Read codeloop.py (219 lines), sandbox.py (87), report.py (69), experiments/figure.py (31), tests/test_sandbox.py (44). Small and readable. Defects: codeloop.py:84-93 monkeypatches mimic-cursor's game.imitate at import time; codeloop.py:173-185 discards the model's reply and source for rejected and losing candidates, so failures cannot be diagnosed (the README admits it does not know which token was banned); sandbox.py:263-264 raises 'banned token' without the token; sandbox.py:235 bans `open` as a bare word anywhere in code, so a variable or keyword argument named open is rejected as unsafe; sandbox.py:265 exposes the whole numpy module, so np.load/np.save/np.fromfile give file access although the docstring and README:16 say no file builtins (README does say it is not a security boundary); Code.imitate (codeloop.py:76-80) silently substitutes the naive bot for crashed strokes up to the 2% cap. report.py:44 hardcodes 4 candidates per round instead of G.BUDGET.
evidence.claims: Checked 8 claims; 6 backed (24 candidates, 7/24 and 6/24 valid, 17/10/8 split, AUROC 1.000 rounds 0-6, component search 1.000 at 24 candidates, ~1 min per candidate). The limits section is candid (one seed, ceiling, sandbox may cause rejections). Not backed or overstated: (1) README:26 'A 1.5B code model mostly fails at the contract' attributes all 35 failures to the model, but 17 are the sandbox's own token ban (unlogged) and 7 of 10 load failures are SyntaxError with max_new_tokens=450 (codeloop.py:139), plausibly truncation by the harness; neither cause was separated, and no repair round was given. (2) README:27 describes the blind final program as 'a random direction added to a line'; it is a line in a near-fixed wrong direction pinned to the end point. (3) README:7 'tied at the ceiling' is accurate but the framing as a comparison oversells it: at 24 candidates the baseline cannot be distinguished from doing nothing (round 0 also 1.000). No prior work for LLM program search is cited, though novelty is not claimed outright.
evidence.fitness: A researcher cannot build on the result: n=1 per condition, every value at AUROC 1.000 including the start program, so the experiment has no power to show anything about code models vs component search or about feedback. Nearest prior work, none cited: FunSearch (Romera-Paredes et al., Nature 2024) and Evolution through Large Models / OpenELM (Lehman et al. 2022) for LLM-written programs selected by a fitness function; Eureka (Ma et al. 2023) for LLM-written reward code refined from feature-level feedback, which is close to the 'feedback' condition; Self-Debugging (Chen et al. 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) and CodeT (Chen et al. 2022) for execution-feedback repair and test-based selection, the standard fix for the 71-75% invalid rate observed here. The finding that a 1.5B model given no error feedback and a 450-token cap produces mostly unusable code is expected from that literature and not new. One session, not part of a multi-session programme; far from the research/CLAUDE.md PhD+ bar.
evidence.domain: A program-synthesis reviewer would reject the design before the numbers: (1) the budget (24 candidates) was chosen where the baseline also cannot move: mimic-cursor's component search stays at 0.998-1.000 at round 6 in all 16 runs and only dips (min 0.82-0.96) later in its 30 rounds, so a tie at the ceiling is guaranteed and uninformative; (2) no execution-feedback repair (errors are not shown to the model, codeloop.py:182-185), no pass@k or valid-rate-by-temperature analysis, and failure causes not logged; (3) harness confounds (sandbox token ban, 450-token cap) not separated from model ability; (4) selection on a 3-feature loop detector with the endpoint pin lets degenerate programs (a line in the wrong direction teleporting to the target) win; (5) one seed, no uncertainty; (6) no comparison with FunSearch/ELM-style islands or best-of-n sampling. The method is a reasonable first harness, not a study a reviewer would sign off on.

defects.what: The comparison is run at a budget (24 candidates) where the baseline cannot move: component search is 0.998-1.000 at round 6 in all 16 runs and the naive start is 1.000, so 'tied at the ceiling' is guaranteed and the study cannot show anything about code models, feedback, or the baseline; one seed per condition, no uncertainty
No execution-feedback repair: rejected or crashing candidates are dropped without showing the error to the model (Self-Debug/Reflexion-style), though invalid code (71-75%) is the study's main finding
Nearest prior work not cited or compared: FunSearch, ELM/OpenELM, Eureka (LLM-written code under fitness/feature feedback), Self-Debugging, Reflexion, CodeT

Headline attributes failures to the model ('mostly fails at the contract') while 17 of 48 are the sandbox's own token ban (token not logged) and 7 are SyntaxErrors under a 450-token cap with replies not saved; harness and model causes are not separated
Model replies and candidate source are not saved, and the banned token is not recorded, so the failure breakdown cannot be audited
Only the sandbox is tested; the failure cap, outcome labelling in report.py and endpoint pin all survive seeded mutations (3 of 4)
Blind final program described as 'a random direction added to a line'; it is a line at a 0-20 degree heading that ignores the target and jumps to the pinned end point (final step median 1.25 chords)
Sandbox exposes the whole numpy module (np.load/np.save/np.fromfile) while the docstring and README say no file access; and bans the bare word 'open' anywhere, rejecting harmless code
Reproduce block says `python3 -m unittest`, which fails without numpy in this container; report.py hardcodes 4 candidates per round instead of G.BUDGET
Planned 3 seeds, 1 ran; no blog post and no PROGRAMMES.md entry

verdict: An honest, small, preliminary negative result whose numbers all reproduce (report and figure byte-identical on rerun; candidate counts, AUROCs and the component-search comparison recomputed from raw JSON; the no-rounding/16 ms claim confirmed by running the final programs). It does not meet the bar: the design cannot discriminate (the chosen 24-candidate budget leaves both the baseline and the naive start at AUROC 1.000, one seed), the main finding (71-75% invalid code) is confounded with the harness (token ban unlogged, 450-token cap, no error-feedback repair) and expected from the self-repair literature, none of the nearest prior work (FunSearch, ELM, Eureka, Self-Debug, Reflexion, CodeT) is cited, and only the sandbox is tested (3 of 4 seeded mutants survive).
